data.text:
Philippines assesses damage after deadly Typhoon Fung-wong.

Powerful storm set off floods and landslides, killing at least two and displacing 1.4 million.

A weakening Typhoon Fung-wong has departed the Philippines after killing at least two people, displacing 1.4 million, and destroying homes and roads across the country’s most populous island.

Rescue workers kicked off recovery efforts on Monday morning across the island of Luzon, home to some 64 million people, as the government lifted all travel restrictions.

Crews wielding power tools, saws and heavy machinery began tackling wreckage, while thousands of Philippine Coast Guard, police and military personnel assumed posts to aid evacuees and assist in rescue operations.

In the eastern coastal town of Dipaculao, where power was still out, footage shared by the local fire agency showed crews using axes to hack through enormous piles of debris – including felled trees and entire metal roofs – as they cleared a roadway.

“We’re seeing many damaged houses and some of our main roads were not passable due to landslides,” rescue worker Geofry Parrocha told the AFP news agency from Dipaculao.

“We couldn’t mobilise last night because the rain was heavy and the volume of water was high,” he said.

The typhoon – which packed winds of 185 kilometres per hour (115 miles per hour) and gusts up to 230km/h (143mph) – made landfall on Aurora province on Sunday evening, unleashing heavy rains and knocking out power to thousands of people.

Even as the storm weakened while moving northwest over the South China Sea, a deluge of up to 200mm (8in) of rain was slated to lash the provinces of La Union, Pangasinan, Benguet and Zambales through Monday, weather bureau PAGASA said. #RUKIGAFMUpdates

𝙁𝙤𝙧 𝙩𝙝𝙚 𝙋𝙚𝙤𝙥𝙡𝙚, 𝙏𝙝𝙧𝙤𝙪𝙜𝙝 𝘼𝙣𝙜𝙖𝙩 𝘽𝙪𝙝𝙖𝙮

As much as we wanted to personally prepare and deliver the relief goods to those affected by the recent typhoons, we decided that it would be best to donate the funds to the Angat Buhay Foundation. 

The weather has been extremely harsh, making it unsafe for us to prepare and transport goods on our own. We understand how dangerous it could be to travel to heavily affected areas, especially with the ongoing situation in nearby provinces. Prioritizing the safety of our members, we have chosen to entrust our donations to a reliable organization like Angat Buhay, which has continuously reached disaster-stricken communities and ensured that relief goods are properly and safely distributed.

Once again, thank you so much to everyone who donated. These combined contributions will go a long way in helping our fellow Filipinos recover and feel cared for during these difficult times. Your generosity means so much. 🫂🩵

We also want to take this opportunity to use our voice as a fandom. The floods and calamities have destroyed homes and lives across the country. But let us continue to remember that we must hold our government officials accountable for what our fellow Filipinos have endured.

Without corruption, the damages could have been less severe. Without corruption, the flooding would not have been this devastating. Without corruption, lives could have been saved. The Philippines could be a better country.

We have been resilient for far too long. Now is the time to hold those in power accountable. Stay angry, stay aware, and never forget.
